subject.title: fix(dispatch-wrapper): fix flock separator and script command detection

question: Should OpenClaw continue failing closed for post-target `flock --` and ambiguous `script --` argv, or add implementation-aware support for a specifically proven wrapper variant?
rationale: The same basename has incompatible command grammars across platforms and versions, and choosing which variants may participate in durable allow-always trust is a security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical parser fix.

options.title: Keep ambiguous forms blocked
options.body: Reject both proposed expansions and preserve the existing conservative approval boundary until a portable contract exists.

options.title: Add implementation-aware parsing
options.body: Support only an executable or platform variant whose exact argv semantics can be identified and covered by real runtime and approval-reuse proof.

options.title: Accept basename-wide semantics
options.body: Merge the generic assumptions and explicitly own the risk that some installed wrappers execute a different target.

recommendation.title: Keep ambiguous forms blocked
recommendation.body: Reject both proposed expansions and preserve the existing conservative approval boundary until a portable contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work established the `flock` security boundary and approval-target compatibility behavior directly changed here.
